When: Within ninety (90) calendar days from the date of contract award. Where: American Center, U.S. Consulate General Chennai, Tamil Nadu, India. Why: To modernize the Center's technological capability with high-end American brand /equivalent hardware that projects a premium, high-tech "American look and

ling flawless technical delivery for public diplomacy programming. Goal: Deploy flexible, multi-modal AV and computing infrastructure that supports formal briefings, large public events, and STEM/makerspace programming. Target Audience: Guests of U.S. Consulate General Chennai, VIP/ executive stakeholders, technical teams, and American Center program attendees & visitors. Primary Objective: Deliver fully tested, IT-cleared, American brand / equivalent technology hardware. f_Work.docx ===== STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) RFID Cabinet The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Health Administration (VHA), requires the acquisition of a Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) storage cabinet integrated with Unique Device Identifier (UDI)-compliant tissue and implant tracking software to support patient safety, regulatory compliance, and efficient inventory management. Tracking tissues, biologics, and implantable medical devices is a federal regulatory requirement under FDA 21 CFR Part 830 (UDI) and is critical to patient safety. VA healthcare facilities face ongoing resource challenges including staff shortages and budget constraints, making it essential to minimize staff time consumed by manual data entry and to maintain precise control over high-value inventory. This acquisition will provide an automated, real-time RFID-based inventory management solution for use in the operating room (OR), Catheterization (Cath) lab, ambulatory surgery center, or any facility location that stores high-value implantable inventory.
